subject.title: [Proposal] Simplify Model Configuration: Single-Source Reconcile + Session Override Reset

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class `openclaw models reconcile` and bulk `openclaw sessions model-reset` commands, or keep this behavior inside the existing doctor/session surfaces and narrower tracked issues?
rationale: The remaining work changes operator-facing config/session semantics across defaults, per-agent overrides, auth profiles, generated catalogs, and persisted sessions; source inspection shows partial mechanisms exist but no single current product boundary owns the proposed workflow.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
options.body: Define the exact reconcile/reset semantics, upgrade behavior, and proof matrix, then implement only the approved subset in core.

options.title: Route to existing surfaces
options.body: Keep using `doctor --fix`, `/model default`, `sessions.patch`, and the narrower open issues, and close or split this umbrella after that decision is explicit.

options.title: Split by failure mode
options.body: Track default-model shadowing, model validation, and session resolver work as separate issues without adding a broad reconcile command now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
recommendation.body: Define the exact reconcile/reset semantics, upgrade behavior, and proof matrix, then implement only the approved subset in core.

likelyOwner.reason: The maintainer-owned session model/auth resolver issue is the closest active product decision surface for the broad session-state portion.
